correctness.rationale: Four independent uniform eccentric anomalies map from the circle to the ellipse by a non-singular diagonal affine map, preserving interior crossing and its 1/3 probability. Conditional on cyclic alternation, normalized consecutive gaps are Dirichlet(1,1,1,1), and the difference Δ between the two circular chord directions satisfies Δ/π~Beta(2,2) with density 6t(π-t)/π³. The affine squared-sine determinant identity and a uniformly convergent Poisson/Fourier expansion reduce the conditional moment to I_j=-3/(π²j²) and the displayed Li₂ formula. The integral for H(x)=((1-x)²/x)Li₂(x) differentiates to a strictly negative integrand, giving dQ/dx<-1/2, unique axis-ratio inversion, quadratic near-circular behavior and the cancellation of the 1/r² slender term. Separate independent beta–Poisson numerical integration matched the Li₂ expression for r=1,1.5,2,5,20 to at most 1.2×10^-14; r=100,1000 crosschecked the logarithmic remainder. Quadrature and asymptotic diagnostics are corroborative, not proofs.

value.rationale: Crossing probability equals 1/3 for every eccentricity, so it contains no shape information; nevertheless the natural orthogonality score E[sin²(angle)|crossing] determines the complete ellipse axis ratio from a single population moment. The strict derivative bound makes inversion well-posed in the shape parameter, while the two degeneration expansions characterize the rigid and slender limits. The result is more than a substitution into a known crossing-frequency formula.
